commander: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse

pilot.summary: Game three of four at Alex's house in Orinda, three-player with Alex and Stuart, on a list five versions behind the one sleeved now. Good hand, dense interaction, and I countered at the right moments — the deck did what it is built to do and still lost. I lost Heliod in a stack war: I countered a spell, Alex countered my counter, I cast Swords to Plowshares and Alex redirected it onto Heliod. Engine offline from there, Psychosis Crawler stranded on the battlefield. My read that night was too many axes and not enough of any one, and that the rebuild direction is protection first.

Second game at Oliver's, four-player with Oliver on Cranko, Alex on a fight deck and Ryan on Scorpion King. Kept three lands, Smothering Tithe, a creature and Long-Term Plans; the Tithe came down early alongside Kami of the Crescent Moon and I was netting about three treasure a cycle — which made me the target with no creatures out. Three sequencing errors: Supreme Verdict after Heliod had resolved, so I killed my own commander; sitting on Long-Term Plans instead of tutoring Approach of the Second Sun to third-from-top; and using the channel-tutor spirit as a blocker rather than a tutor. Oliver assembled his one-card Cranko line while the table beat on me. Loss.

read.what_it_does: No game has been played on the list sleeved now, v1.3.0 (V11). Both logged games sit on earlier lists: 001 on V5, 002 on V10, one set of swaps behind. What those games showed is a resource deck that wants to live long enough to cast Approach of the Second Sun: Smothering Tithe and Kami of the Crescent Moon down early, about three treasure a cycle, and Long-Term Plans in hand to put Approach third from the top (002). The mana half worked; the finish never happened because I sat on the tutor (002). The hand-size punisher axis has not converted in either game: Psychosis Crawler was on the battlefield with the pieces to grow it and never got there (001), and after 002 I wrote that the axis needed too many pieces and only ever pinged. Every card the two notes name is still in the 99, so the lessons carry; the three cards v1.3.0 cut appear in neither note.
read.how_it_plays: Slow and visible, and it ends up as the seat the table beats on. Smothering Tithe made me the target immediately with no creatures out (002, on V10). Both games ended with somebody else closing while I was still assembling: a stack war took Heliod and the engine went offline (001, on V5, before the protection passes), and Oliver put together a one-card Cranko line while the table hit me (002). My own cross-game note is that momentum, tempo and table optics are the recurring gap and that it is me rather than the deck, and that I avoid this deck partly because blue-white control feels intimidating (002). Whether three free artifact casts change the tempo is untested; nothing on v1.3.0 has been played yet.
mindful_of: Wipe first, then resolve Heliod. Supreme Verdict came down after the commander and killed it (002). Both cards are still in the list.

Long-Term Plans is a tutor, and it wants using early. I overthought the cost of Approach of the Second Sun (with the treasure and the discount it is two or three, not seven), waited, got desperate, and the window closed (002).

Deploy Smothering Tithe behind blockers, or hold it until there are some. It bought the whole table's attention while my board was empty (002). v1.3.0 cut Angelic Wall; the branch note says the taxers and the counterspells are the defence now, so the shell has to be those.
The channel-tutor spirit is a tutor first. I used it as a blocker, caught between surviving and assembling, and took the short-term play (002).
There is no pressure to rush the commander out in this build, and I keep acting as though there is (002).
The commander going away takes the engine with it. That was the stack war on V5 (001) and my own wipe on V10 (002).

Symmetric card draw arms the table against me. That read was made on V5 and the list it was read against is superseded, but Kami of the Crescent Moon is still the early engine piece and was on the table in 002, and v1.3.0 adds Horn of Greed, which draws each player a card on a land drop. It still applies (001, 002).
The hand-size punisher axis has not paid in either game (001, 002). v1.3.0 took Forced Fruition out; Psychosis Crawler stays.
read.what_changed: The games sit on V5 (001) and V10 (002); the list sleeved today is V11, v1.3.0, and no game has been played on it. Between the two games the paper list was checked in at V6 with fifteen swaps and the combo it no longer runs, then lynchpin-v1, skies-v1 and archangel-v1 landed; the version notes call those the commander getting a bodyguard and a backup plan, a board that can finally block what kills it, and one flier gained. That was 001's conclusion, protection before more axes, acted on. 002 did not test it: I lost Heliod to my own Supreme Verdict rather than to a stack war, and had nothing on board when the Tithe drew fire (002). v1.3.0 is three swaps from the artifacts-v1 branch, all owned generic-cost artifacts the flipped Heliod casts for free: Isochron Scepter for Mikaeus, the Lunarch (thirteen instants at two or less to imprint; the branch note says the Scepter is a free cast under the discount, its activation is not), Horn of Greed for Forced Fruition (a card for each player on a land drop, which the branch reads as a discount for me on each opponent's turn, where the flash deck casts), and Mind Stone for Angelic Wall (ramp stays in band). The branch objective was a control, because the goldfish reads none of the six cards, so the case is the argued one and the games are what will settle it. Two of the swaps point where 002 pointed: Horn of Greed is the research item I asked for, more ways to turn opponents' card draw into value, and cutting Forced Fruition stops feeding the hand-size punisher axis (002). The branch case for the Scepter is a counterspell every turn for two mana; 001 was lost to a counter war, so that is the first thing to watch in the first game on v1.3.0 (001).
